messages:
Build "Reading Companion": an AI research agent that reads arXiv papers with the user and answers questions about them, with sources. The agent must plan, call tools, read, and check its own answer; a plain chat box is not enough.

Users: students and researchers who need to understand a paper fast and know exactly where each statement comes from.

Flow:
1. Home: a goal box ("What do you want to know?"), an optional arXiv id or link, and three one-click example goals (for example: "What is the main result of arXiv 1607.01759 and how was it measured?", "Find recent papers on isolation forest anomaly detection and compare their claims", "Does arXiv 2601.03664 release code and which datasets does it use?").
2. The agent works in visible steps: Plan (3 to 5 bullet steps), Tool calls, Notes, Answer, Self-check. Show each tool call with its arguments and a short result preview in a timeline, live as it happens. Maximum 12 agent turns.
3. Tools the agent can call (OpenAI function tools via the LLM gateway):
   - search_arxiv(query, limit) -> list of {id, title, authors, published, summary}
   - get_abstract(id) -> {id, title, authors, published, summary}
   - read_paper(id, offset) -> {text, next_offset, total_chars}; the text comes in slices of about 9000 characters and the agent decides whether to read more.
   - note(text): saves a short finding with a source (paper id and a quote of at most 25 words) to a notes panel.
4. Final answer: a concise answer in the selected language with numbered citations [1], [2] that link to arXiv; every claim must be backed by a note. Then a "Self-check" step: the agent re-reads its notes and lists anything it could not verify or that is only in the abstract, and marks those claims "unverified".
5. Notes and sources panel on the right (below the timeline on mobile): every note with paper id, quote, and a link.
6. Save finished sessions in the Atoms Cloud database (goal, answer, notes, tokens) and show a public "Recent questions" gallery; a session has a share link.

Backends (already built, do not change them, never put keys in the app):
- LLM gateway: POST https://vzvyghmtsakixlhzzuol.supabase.co/functions/v1/agent-llm with {"app":"companion","visitor":"<random id in localStorage>","messages":[...],"tools":[...],"max_tokens":2000}. Returns {"message":{role,content,tool_calls},"finish_reason","usage"}. HTTP 429 means a rate limit: show a friendly message.
- Paper tools: POST https://vzvyghmtsakixlhzzuol.supabase.co/functions/v1/paper-tools with {"action":"search","query":"...","limit":6}, {"action":"abstract","id":"1607.01759"} or {"action":"text","id":"1607.01759","offset":0}. Some papers have no HTML version; then the agent should say so and use the abstract only.

Design: clean, professional, calm blue and neutral palette, serif headline (Fraunces) with IBM Plex Sans body, generous spacing, no emoji, light and dark mode, mobile friendly (no horizontal scroll at 390px). English and Chinese with a language toggle (EN / 中文) for all interface text; the agent answers in the selected language.
I'll start by setting up the full-stack template, because saved sessions and the public gallery need the Atoms Cloud database.
Next I'll read the backend and frontend READMEs before writing any code.
Next I'm reading the Web SDK and custom API guides, and checking which tables already exist.
I'll create the public sessions table first, since the data contract has to exist before I build the gallery and share pages.
I'm checking the generated sessions router for its auth requirements and looking at the frontend source layout.
Next I'll check whether the generated routes need auth, and test the two external backends with quick requests.
I'll read the remaining output from the backend tests.
I'm calling the LLM gateway directly with a short timeout to confirm its response shape.
I've confirmed how both external backends respond. Next I'll check two dependency details, then write the core libraries: translations, the agent loop and session storage.
Both backends work as expected. A paper with no HTML version returns a 404 error saying it is PDF only. Next I'll write the theme tokens, translations, agent engine and session storage.
Next I'll build the interface: the header, the shared timeline and notes view, the home page, the shared-session page and the routes.
I'll swap the dynamic import in the home page for a static one, then run lint and build.
Lint and build both pass. Next I'll record the architecture in the project notes, then check how the UI renders.
The "Recent questions" section shows a load error, so I'll test the sessions endpoint on the backend directly.
I'll query the local sessions API directly to find out why the gallery failed to load.
The sessions table exists in the schema, but the running local database hasn't picked it up yet. I'll check the migration setup before applying it.
I'll check whether the existing migration includes the sessions table, then apply migrations to the local database.
The migration failed because the database URL isn't set in this shell, so I'll find which URL the running backend uses and check how the migration reads it.
The migration setup skips any table named "sessions" (it treats that name as legacy), so that table will never be created. I'll recreate it under a new name, `reading_sessions`.
The new table is in place, so next I'll check it responds and point the frontend's storage code at it.
I've pointed the frontend at the new table. Next I'll test a save-and-delete on the backend, update the architecture notes, and re-run lint and build.
The gallery error is fixed: the backend round trip works and lint and build pass. Next I'll log progress in the project notes.
I'm adding the progress entries to the project notes before wrapping up.

Reading Companion is built, and you can open it in App Viewer. Lint and the build pass, and the home page renders as designed. I tested the arXiv tools, the AI gateway and saving a session separately, but I haven't run a full question from start to finish, so that's the first thing to try.

**How it works:**
- **Home:** the goal box, an optional arXiv id or link, and the three example goals, each of which starts with one click.
- **Live timeline:** the agent shows its Plan (3–5 steps), then each tool call with its arguments and a short result preview as it happens. It reads papers in slices of about 9,000 characters, decides whether to read more, and stops at 12 turns.
- **Notes panel:** on the right (below the timeline on phones). Each note has the paper id, a quote of at most 25 words and an arXiv link. The app checks each quote against the text the agent actually fetched and labels it "Full text", "Abstract only" or "Quote not found".
- **Answer:** written in the selected language, with numbered citations that link to arXiv. If a paper has no HTML version, the agent is told to say so and use the abstract only.
- **Self-check:** the agent re-reads its notes. Any claim that is uncited, rests only on the abstract, has a quote that wasn't found, or cites a note that doesn't exist is marked "unverified", both in the answer and in the self-check list.
- **Saving and sharing:** finished sessions are saved with the goal, answer, notes and token counts. They appear in the public "Recent questions" gallery and get a share link (`/s/…`) with a copy button. Sessions you stop partway are not saved.
- **Errors:** if either service returns a rate limit, a friendly "busy, try again in a minute" message appears.

**Design:** Fraunces headlines with IBM Plex Sans body text in a calm blue and neutral palette, an EN / 中文 toggle for all interface text, light and dark mode, no emoji, and a layout built for 390px phones.

**Changes from what you might expect:**
- **The agent runs in the browser.** It calls your two backends directly and unchanged, and no keys are in the app.
- **The database table is named `reading_sessions`.** The backend's database setup skips any table named "sessions", so that name would never have been created.

Next, publish the app and share the link, and tell me if anything looks wrong or doesn't behave as expected.
